ResponsesInList.Title: Release of STACK 3.6 and STACK 4.0.
ResponsesInList.Text: It gives me great pleasure to announce the release of two new versions of STACK . ** STACK 3.6 ** STACK 3.6 represents a major new release.  The most significant feature is the new "line by line working". This enables students to solve an equation (or simple real single variable inequality) by progressively transforming their expression.  STACK accepts the entire argument, and establishes various properties such as "are all lines equivalent?", "is the last line in 'solved' form?" and so on.  I will write more about this feature in a separate email, but it represents the first significant step into full automation of students' free-form working. These features include a very large (bewildering perhaps) array of design choices.  I have released a *minimum* working product which automates line by line reasoning.  The intention is to work with students and teachers over the next year to identify the key features needed, and the most sensible ways of using this facility.  For example, is immediate feedback on each line of working actually helpful, or just a distraction?  We need to undertake some detailed research to better understand these issues, and I would very much welcome collaboration in pursing this aspect of online assessment use. ** STACK 4.0 ** STACK 4.0 represents a major new release and brings important developments in a parallel fork of STACK back into the main master branch.  These developments have been written by colleagues at Aalto in Finland, and I am very grateful for there significant contributions and ongoing collaboration.   These features have been widely tested in the parallel fork of STACK. In addition to the features in STACK 3.6, STACK 4.0 adds "question blocks".  Question blocks are conditional statements within the CAS text.  This will allow the text seen by students to adapt in highly non-trivial ways to the random variables, with whole blocks of text being revealed or hidden.  Looping structures enable the automatic generation of code which can be interpreted by Javascript which generates diagrams.  The architecture of the question blocks is very flexible and extensible.  I am only now beginning to appreciate the possibilities of this design.  Watch this space. STACK 4.0 is tagged as v4.0 and is available from the master branch.  This will be installed by default as it is the branch being supporting in the future. ** Why two separate releases? ** For the first time in many years we have changed some of the question authoring mechanism in STACK.  Instead of including CAS statements with @...@ question authors are now required to use {@...@}.  The extra curly braces enable better matching, and more reliable parsing which were essential in the question block engineering.  We have also introduced {#...#} to embed the *Maxima value* and not the *LaTeX representation.  For example, {@sin(n%pi)@}-> \sin(n\pi) whereas {#sin(n*%pi)#} -> sin(n*pi).  This is essential for communication with other software (e.g. chart generation) which needs a more formal syntax and does not accept LaTeX. Users upgrading from STACK 3.X to STACK 4.0 will find that existing questions need to be converted to the new syntax before they will function correctly.  We have developed an automatic conversion script which I have used reliably on our materials, but this is such an important step that I have decided to enforce a manual review before converted questions are saved.  Therefore, admins upgrading servers will need to work with question authors to facilitate this change! ** Future plans ** The University of Edinburgh will be using STACK 4.0 in the 2017-18 academic cycle.  I will support STACK 3.6 over the next academic cycle with bug fixes etc.  Anyone requiring support for STACK 3.X beyond June 2018 should contact me privately to discuss this further.  New features will only be added (by me) to STACK 4.X, Bug fixes etc. will be supported here: https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/tree/version3.6 While the line by line features will undergo further active development over the next year (and hence may change in STACK 4.1) the other features, including the blocks, are stable and I hope existing users continue to find STACK a useful and reliable assessment tool. I'd like to thank the team of translators who have translated the language packs in the STACK plugin. I very much welcome collaboration, and contributions.  Examples of questions, research studies, contributions to the documentation (e.g. examples of how to author particular questions) are easy to contribute without having to develop code. Comments welcome. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: STACK Matrix input type creates new lines
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thomas, Yes, this is very annoying.  I consider it a bug in STACK, but the truth is that the bug is caused by a subtle interaction between STACK, the editor, the MathJax filter and other clean up code in Moodle. Imagine we have the following question text ```text ```

Find vectors so that \( v = \lambda_1 \) input:ans1 \(+\lambda_2 \) input:ans2

validation:ans1 validation:ans2

In the various transformations between the teacher and the students the "inputs" get replaced by tables, and the maths text gets processed by the mathjax filter.  This leads to spans with class "filter_mathjaxloader_equation" containing an opening paragraph

, but with the span closing before the table for the input.   We get something like this ```text

Find vectors so that \( v = \lambda_1 \) .... ``` Then later in Moodle, the closing

is inserted by some later Moodle cleaning up code.  All very helpful, but it breaks the display! One way to avoid (workaround) the problem is to switch off the TinyMCE editor: go to ' Administration > Site administration > Plugins > Text editors > Manage editors ' Then don't use paragraph (`

`) tags in your question text. This is all very well until someone comes along and edits the question later and the editor puts back in paragraph tags for you.... I would very much appreciate some help here from people with more knowledge of Moodle about how STACK can adapt to stop this bug.  Any suggestions?  Sorry I don't know more about the text editors and filters in Moodle to know exactly what to do here. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Plotting lg with STACK fails
ResponsesInList.Text: Stefan, Thank you very much indeed for reporting this bug.  I'm very sorry we omitted to anticipate this when we introduce the "logbase" functionality.  This is one consequence of having "ephemeral" forms which represent by don't simplify.  At some point, the lack of simplification comes back to get you... A fix is here: https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/issues/298 I've added this to the "equiv_input" branch  as I'm in the final testing phases of this code for a major new release.  I can't see a reason why this small change can't be added to your code individually if you really need it immediately. An immediate workaround should be to use `@plot(ev(lg(x), logbase=logbasesimp), [x, -.5,5])@` Thanks again for the report, much appreciated. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: WIRIS breaks MathML?
ResponsesInList.Text: WIRIS plugin stores formulas in Moodle with a slightly modified MathML code that we call safeXML. SafeXML is plain MathML changing some characters: http://www.wiris.com/en/plugins/docs/resources/encoding-attributes . You can configure the plugin to store formulas as MathML instead of safeXML setting wiriseditorsavemode= xml in your plugin's configuration.ini file ( http://www.wiris.com/plugins/docs/resources/configuration-table ). In order to edit the formulas using WIRIS you need to keep both WIRIS and MathJax filters enabled, however, due to an issue with Moodle's filter order in combination with our plugin and MathJax, you need to manually uncomment the filter in /wiris/filter.php. Please note that this is a workaround until we fix the order issue in future WIRIS plugin versions.

Wait a bit for the new pool to start up. If you keep reloading the status page, you should see the number of active processes go up to whatever value you set. Click the "Run the high-level health-check" button for the newly started pool to verify that that works. Click back again. Only  then try to evaluate 1+1 using the form on the status page.

There is even better documentation there (I hope) https://github.com/maths/stack_util_maximapool/tree/multiple-pools/doc . It should not be that hard to get Tomcat installed and running by following the instructions you can find online. I guess I could save you the effort of compiling the code. The two folders WEB-INF and META-INF should be at the top level of the zip file, I think.) Rename back to MaximaPool.war. Use that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Stack, MaximaPool and Maxima on a separate server
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't think you should replace the original Maxima executable. The MaximaPool configuration file lets you give a path to the executable to run. Configure it to point to the maxima-optimised you built wherever you saved it. maxima-optimised starts faster. As you say, for a single user, using un-optimised maxima is OK, because the STACK user does not notice the start-up time. However, when you have many students attempting a quiz at the same time, all the work of staring maxima will be happening on the MaximaPool server, and that will slow things down. For that reason it is worth optimising the start-up of each process. All MaximaPool is really doing is running maxima like a command-line tool, piping in input, and capturing the output. So, you can directly simulate that on the command-line (even more-so if you sudo so the web-server user). That is a good way to debug problems. Also in the MaximaPool interface (if you go there in your web browser) there are the 'healthcheck' links. The Low-level healthcheck shows you exactly what happens as maxima-pool tries to run one command using your configuration one step at a time (making a new process, not taking one form the pool). The High-level healthcheck tests what happens when MaximaPool gets a request from STACK. It takes a process from the pool and uses it. (Those debugging tools exist because they are what were needed to get things working myself.) I hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: quiz_stack required ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris and Tim, Thanks a lot to continue Stack's development. What about quiz_stack file for the last version of Stack ? I updated my Stack version, linux optimised, and it works fine, but I see on the plugins page that the quiz_stack file isn't on the hard drive. Is this file required for full features of stack ? Thanks a lot. Laurent from France

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: quiz_stack required ?
ResponsesInList.Text: It is optional. It is an extra quiz report that might help you if you want to dive into the details of all the responses all students gave to your questions, but you don't need it. Since you can install it at any time, perhaps best to start without it. The standard quiz reports tell you almost everything you want to know anyway.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: quiz_stack required ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, this is optional. Also, there is a lot left to do with the quiz_stack plugin. If anyone would like to contribute something to this project then comprehensive reporting would be welcome. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Chemistry editor
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi! I have installed chemistry editor ( https://moodle.org/plugins/atto_chemistry ) and have very interesting problems that I don't know have to solve. Output pictures are changing over time. First it is like this Thank after few seconds: Then after 27 seconds: Does somebody have some explanation what is going on? Thank you. Ivica

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Chemistry editor
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Ivica, The images are produced by Moodle text filters that are enabled on the page rather that the by the editor directly. It appears that both the TeX notation filter and the MathJax filter are enabled on the page you are seeing. The first image is produced by the TeX filter on the server . The TeX filter is normally much faster than MathJaX, but does not match as closely to the surrounding text as well as MathJax. The next two images that appear are produced by MathJax in your browser. The second is and rough preview that MathJax does quickly. It then takes another pass and displays the final image when it is finished. These results may depend in your case whether the mhchem package or extension is enabled and whether there is fonts are available. You can control which images are produced depending on what you want to happen. If you are happy with the first image, you can disable the MathJax filter on the page and the TeX filter image will remain. You can also control how MathJax is displayed by right clicking the final image and choosing changing the renderer option. It looks like MathJax is missing the mhchem extension. To fix that you would need to change the MathJax filter configuration. Daniel

ResponsesInList.Text: I am looking for something, that is probably not a STACK or math topic but a general moodle thing. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Drill Excerises?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hendrikje, I think you are asking for a particular kind of "quiz engine" here?  Is this a single question quiz? STACK certainly has the potential to provide "within question" random versions, but so do other question types."Try another version" seems a sensible option for a single question quiz.  Do you want to link questions together? If so, how will you link together questions once a student has completed one? I agree that the current Moodle quiz has some restrictions which I don't like.   Can you specify more clearly what you do want? I should add, that much can be done with the Moodle quiz by adding in "Description" questions.  The CodeRunner people showed me almost complete courses which were Moodle quizzes with the academic content provided by Description questions embedded in the quiz. I've done this for teachers with my demo quiz but lacked the courage with my own courses for students! I just post PDF notes... This is a challenging perspective. Should we put questions inside materials, or materials inside quizzes? We should discuss architecture of what we really need, so if you could describe a use case this would kick things off. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Drill Excerises?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, at the moment I am thinking about quizzes in Classes and not the other way around since our moodle class is an addition to lectures and study groups at university. But the "class in quiz" sounds rether interesting. Until now, I only knew complete classes that were SCORM -Modules. We try to provide materials for linear algebra. Using the quizzes I know, we can give them some sort of worksheet they need to complete to have it graded. (Or, with different options, they can get feedback directly after they did one of the questions.) But they will always have to finish the quiz to get a new one. Thats ok for some complicated questions they will do once or maybe twice. But what I am thinking about is really a different type of quiz, that will generate questions one after another. For example: They get a complex number in polar coordinates and need to calculate the rectangular ones. Something really easy and fast forward but students still got trouble with it, so they better do it like10 times, 20 times... With the quiz-engine at the moment I can give them this question once, then they will have to restart the quiz every time, but that way they will probably do it five times at the most. The other version would be: One quiz with the same question over and over again. This seems to be a little better but rather tedious for the students who understand the whole thing. So, what I'd love to have is to have this one question in thiz mini-quiz, they can ask for a new version or to stop the excersise at any point, after answering a question, they would get instant feedback about their result and at the end they might get a small chart how many answers were correct, how many questions were skipped, etc. As far as I can see, the main difference to the existing quizzes is the variable amount of questions, everything else seems to be possible already. I was asking for more than one question in the begining, because sometimes you've got rather similar problems, and constructing two different questions would be easier, than putting everything in one question: For example working with systems of equations. I can construct "nice" systems, that have one, none or an infinite number of solutions. So that are actually three questions but they could all go in the same mini-quiz ans sometimes the student will have system a, sometimes system b. Helpful feedback would be a lot easyier, since the feedback could be different depending on the problem...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Drill Excerises?
ResponsesInList.Text: In general, it will work. Within the code, there is a good separation between question types, and activities that use questions, which means that if an activity works well with one question type, then it will work well with all of them. However, there is one detail of that which Question practice does not handle yet - internal random variants. In Moodle, if you have 10 similar muliple-choice questions, then those will be 10 different questions in a category in the question bank. However, with STACK (and other similar question types like the core Calculated types) one question in the question bank can have 10 different internal variants. Question practice does not really understand that yet. In an ideal world it would. In terms of the code, this would require some small changes to the functions like get_next_question and choose_other_question ( https://github.com/marcusgreen/moodle-mod_qpractice/blob/qp_1.2/locallib.php#L148 and https://github.com/marcusgreen/moodle-mod_qpractice/blob/qp_1.2/locallib.php#L116 ). I am not sure if this theoretical lack in the code will have a significant impact on students or not. It is well worth trying it and seeing. If you do try it, please let us know how it goes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Stack for test for convergence and divergence
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thanks for your kind comments about STACK . I think this is a Maxima question, rather than a STACK one, but I'll do my best. In Maxima the following happens 
```text
integrate(1/x,x,1,inf);


defint: integral is divergent.
```
 So the problem is that you want to catch an error. What we need is a function like the following in this file: https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/blob/master/stack/maxima/stackmaxima.mac 
```text
integrablep(ex,v,a,b):=block([res], 


  res:errcatch(integrate(ex,v,a,b)),


  print("STACK: ignore previous error."),


  if is(res=[]) then return(false),


  return(true)


)$
```
 However, this relies on Maxima's integrate function.  I don't know how reliable this would be. Lastly, when I come up against this kind of issue, I generally solve the problem by very careful randomisation rather than leaving this to chance.  Is there a reason why you can't start with known integrable/non-integrable things? Also, do you have a list of more specific test cases? Chris

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello Daniel Thanks for your help! I was able to solve the problem! It was a permission error and I had to set a SEBool, in order to reenable SELinux. The error was caused because the apache user had no permissions on the /usr/lib64/maxima folder and the /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised file. Following permissions can be used on CentOS 7 to make STACK work: 
```text

```
 Enable SELinux Bool 
```text
setsebool -P httpd_execmem 1
```
 Set Permissions 
```text
setfacl -b --recursive /usr/lib64/maxima/
setfacl -b --recursive /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised
chown -R root:root /usr/lib64/maxima/

setfacl --recursive --modify user:root:rwX /usr/lib64/maxima/
setfacl --recursive --modify default:user:root:rwX /usr/lib64/maxima/

setfacl --recursive --modify user:apache:rwX /usr/lib64/maxima/
setfacl --recursive --modify default:apache:rwX /usr/lib64/maxima/


setfacl --recursive --modify user::rwX /usr/lib64/maxima/
setfacl --recursive --modify default:user::rwX /usr/lib64/maxima/

setfacl --recursive --modify group::r-X /usr/lib64/maxima/
setfacl --recursive --modify default:group::r-X /usr/lib64/maxima/

setfacl --recursive --modify other:r-X /usr/lib64/maxima/

setfacl --recursive --modify default:other:r-X /usr/lib64/maxima/

setfacl --modify user:root:rwx  /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised 

setfacl --modify user:apache:r--  /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised 

setfacl --modify group::r--  /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised 

setfacl  --modify other:r--  /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised 
restorecon -Frv /usr/lib64/maxima-optimised 
restorecon -Frv /usr/lib64/maxima/
```

I do have plans to include GeoGebra within STACK and use the javascript interface to interrogate the applet and return a mathematical expression.  A colleague did get this working, which is great but I've not had time to investigate this fully and document it. I don't immediately see how we would end up with a CAS expression.  As Tim suggests, there is probably a role for a dedicated input type here and an extension to STACK which can properly evaluate the data it returns. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Square Roots and STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, It appears that Maxima favors fractional powers over the radical sign. However, it is extremely common (and expected) in high school and lower college-level mathematics classes to use the radical sign over fractional powers. My problem is that it appears that there's no way for me to check that a student "simplifies" a square root fully in the usual way for this level of math. In this level of simplification, all powers inside the radical must be strictly less than the index of the radical, in other words, in fractional power notation, the fractional exponent is a "proper fraction".... Is there any way to do this in STACK currently?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Square Roots and STACK
ResponsesInList.Text:
Stuart, This is a very good point. STACK currently supports two notations for the same (?) thing. Syntax such as "sqrt(x)" which gives surds Fractional powers, such as "x^(1/2)" which uses index notation. There is an option in the question to control the display of expressions in the question variables (regardless of which form is being used). There are ways to check if the student has simplified, but these might not be what you want. STACK does not have a "general purpose simplify" test, with feedback, since I don't think we would ever agree what that means!  Perhaps we can work from specific examples? The "EqualsComAss" test (equality up to commutativity and associativity) will establish that x^(2/4) is not the same as x^(1/2) but "AlgEquiv" will establish they are equivalent.   You can use the "lowest terms" to give feedback that x^(2/4) contains a fraction not in lowest terms. Your specific example is something like sqrt(x^2)?  What would you accept here, x or abs(x)?  The AlgEquiv test considers x, sqrt(x^2) to be different, and abs(x) and sqrt(x^2) to be equivalent. By default, Maxima does the following: 
```text
sqrt(x^2) -> abs(x)


sqrt(x^6) -> x^2*abs(x)
```
 etc.  If you assume(x>0) (or choose the option Assume positive at the question level in the options) then you'll get something closer to what you want. 
```text
sqrt(x^2) -> x


sqrt(x^6) -> x^3
```
 "rootscontract" is a potentially useful maxima function in this context .  See also "radexpand". If you have sqrtdispflag:false; then 
```text
sqrt(x^3) -> (x^3)^(1/2).
```
 In this case you can use the function "radcan" to get x^(3/2).  I can't see an easy way to transform (x^a)^b -> x^(a*b) and the rule n/m*a/b -> (n*a)/(m*b) without cancelling fractions to lowest terms.  I think you are about to ask me how to do that as well?! If you have specific examples of things you do and don't want to be equal, let me know and I'll figure out how to do it. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Square Roots and STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: Very helpful information about what's going on. And I absolutely understand the difficulty associated with notation and  the notion of what "simplified" even means, and the confounding fact that different maturity levels in mathematics dictates different definitions for simplification. To that end, I agree that a general purpose simplification is too broad to implement. To my specific case, I am teaching an Algebra 2 remedial class and we are approaching completing the square, so to do that, I'm having to review the Algebra I concept of simplifying radical expressions. I wanted them to, for instance, "simplify" \( \sqrt{8} \) and give me the answer \( 2\sqrt{2} \) . I know maxima sees/works with it as \( 2^(3/2) \) instead. And that's fine. But I don't want to allow them to simply type \( \sqrt{8} \) as the answer. And I'm betting there's a way to disallow this using two decision trees, I just don't know which test(s) to use to do so. Further, with radicals that have multiple squares in them, I want all of the squares pulled outside the radical. For instance, \( \sqrt{80} \) should induce an answer of \( 4\sqrt{5} \) , but should only give partial credit for \( 2\sqrt{20} \) . And I'm afraid if there is a solution that checks the exact display between the two, the first example of \( \sqrt{8} \) proves problematic then since maxima turns that into an improper rational power. If it's not possible, that's okay, I can work around it. I'm just befuddled.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Square Roots and STACK
ResponsesInList.Text:
Ok, the attached question is a start here. I've switched off question level simplification, to keep expressions unchanged, and then defined the following question variables to reverse engineer the problem. 
```text
a:2


b:2


m:ev(a*b^2,simp)


ta:a*sqrt(b)


p:sqrt(m);
```
 The only sensible question text I can think of is the following: 
```text
Re-write @p@ in the form 
\(a\sqrt{b}\)
 where 
\(b\)
 is an integer which is a product of primes. 
input:ans1
 
validation:ans1
```
 (I know the product of primes bit is probably *not* what you had in mind for your class, but I think that is what you mean?  How else do you describe this form?  "square free"?) The potential response tree also switches off simplification.  We then basically to the following. 
```text
1. ATEqualComAss(ans1, ta)?   True=>stop.  False=>2.
2. ATAlgEquiv(ans1, ta)? True=> 3. False=>stop + feedback.
3. ATEqualComAss(ans1, p)? True=>stop + feedback (you didn't do anything!)
4. ATEqualComAss(ans1, ev(radcan(p),simp))? Checks to see if a student used fractional powers, i.e typed in 2^(3/2).
```
 Other tests are possible, but I think this gives a decent coverage of the possible cases.  You could probably change the order of 2 & 3 to catch the case of \(2\sqrt{4}\) .  Is there anything else you'd like to test for? I think a lot of people are befuddled by square roots and fractional powers in general.  I've become slightly obsessed by it as a topic in elementary maths.  I think it is really interesting but dinner beckons..... Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Subscripts in STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear all, I've received a new feature request to support subscripts in STACK .  That is, entry and manipulation of expressions such as \(a_b\) .  I propose to accept these with an input syntax a_b There will be no especial meaning to this, it is just a notational device.  Does anyone have any comments about this? Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscripts in STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: Chris, The ability to use both letters and numbers as subscripts in algebraic expressions is of critical importance for our use of STACK in physics problems. We often require use of variables with one or two subscripts involving both letters and numbers, such as:  a x ,  F 1x ,  V 2y . It will be important that all types of subscripts be entered the same way, whether the subscript is a single number, single letter, or a combination of letters and numbers. The proposed input syntax of   a_b   should work just fine, as long as   a_bc   can also be used, where    bc   could be any combination of letters and numbers. Presently with STACK, a number immediately following a variable is automatically interpreted as a subscript. It might be wise to remove this feature and require the underscore format for all subscripts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscripts in STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks David, We can certainly define an operator which has no function definition.  Then, we can use this to fine-tune the display.  I think that we could use the underscore character here. Does anyone object to expanding the Maxima input syntax to allow underscore characters as an inert function which is displayed as subscript? Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscripts in STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: There is some further discussion about the use of subscripts in Maxima on the mailing list here: https://sourceforge.net/p/maxima/mailman/maxima-discuss/thread/slrnn6mul0.6s4.robert.dodier%40freekbox.fglan/#msg34689050 Adding in subscripts is not as straightforward as I originally thought, partly because the underscore character is already accepted, but the result (e.g. a_b) is considered by Maxima to be a single atom, and not two atoms connected by an operator. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscripts in STACK
ResponsesInList.Text: Tim, The solution here is to use the binomial function and use Maxima's "tex" function.  Maxima already does this ```text binomial(n,a)$ tex(%); ``` ```text $${{n}\choose{a}}$$ ``` If you'd really like the form \({}^{n} C_{i}\) then we just redefine TeX's command in Maxima: ```text binomialtex(e) := block ([a, b],     [a, b]:args (e),     concat("{}^{",tex1(a),"}C_{",tex1(b),"}") )$ texput(binomial, binomialtex)$ ``` ```text tex(binomial(n,c)); $${}^{n}C_{c}$$ ``` This is all pure Maixma, but STACK will respect this. There are plenty of other examples of this fine-tuning of the display already. (Teachers are not currently permitted to use texput, but I think we could change that or add this style as an option.) Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting GnuPlot graphs out of the STACK question type
ResponsesInList.Text: You may think it is odd, but there is a logical explanation. The URL that you eventually need to use to serve the image is [ http://your.moodle ]/question/type/stack/plot.php/[image name]. However, there is no need for the MaximaPool server to have to deal with that. Therefore, STACK tells MaximaPool to put !ploturl! into the HTML where the path "[ http://your.moodle ]/question/type/stack/plot.php" needs to go. Then, when the question is displayed to students, STACK does a search and replace on the question text. This probably means that, if you put the string !ploturl! in your question text, a weird thing will happen when you attempt the question, but I doubt anyone will ever have a legitimate reason to do that.

ResponsesInList.Title: STACK: Paired Random Variables
ResponsesInList.Text: In our use of STACK we often use multiple random variables within the question. Is there a way to generate paired random variables in which only predetermined paired values are displayed? For example, one might have the following random variables: x : rand([ 1,3,5 ]); y : rand([ 2,4,6 ]); However, only particular pairings of x and y are acceptable for the problem, say: x : 1 , y : 2 x : 3 , y : 4 x : 5 , y : 6 Is there a function that can be used to accomplish this? ResponsesInList.Text:
If you would like to update STACK on Centos 6, you can build your own RPM with the following procedure I used. Download maxima-5.31.3-1.src.rpm to home directory along with the attached patch file. Then on command line do the following 
```text
sudo yum install sbcl texinfo rpm-build
cd ~
rpm -i maxima-5.31.3-1.src.rpm
cd rpmbuild/SPECS
patch maxima.spec <~/patch
rpmbuild -ba maxima.spec
```
 If no other packages need to be added this should generate what you need in ~/rpmbuild/RPMS.  (Note only yum is run as root)

ResponsesInList.Title: Building maxima package on Centos for STACK
ResponsesInList.Text:
I found a slightly simpler approach for creating maxima packages off CENTOS. I am documenting it here for upgrades. Instead of downloading the original maxima src, the src rpms from the Fedora distribution can be used. For example 
```text
sudo yum install sbcl texinfo rpm-build
cd ~


wget 
http://dl.fedoraproject.org/pub/fedora/linux/updates/22/SRPMS/m/maxima-5.36.1-2.fc22.src.rpm


rpm -i maxima-5.36.1-2.fc22.src.rpm
cd rpmbuild


rpmbuild -ba SPECS/maxima.spec


cd RPMS/x86_64


sudo yum remove maxima


sudo yum install maxima-runtime-sbcl-5.36.1-2.el6.x86_64.rpm maxima-5.36.1-2.el6.x86_64.rpm
```
 CENTOS 7 does not have a maxima package in the EPEL repo, but this is how EPEL packages are  produced.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Jaya Prakash. I'm sorry but I don't understand your question.  Are you writing the formula in notepad and want to import into Moodle?    Moodle has an in-built editor, so you should be able to cut-and-paste any LaTeX formula into Moodle and use one of the filters (e.g. MathJax) to display it.  Many people do this, so this forum will be able to help you. If you are trying to copy the formula from Moodle to Notepad, then many people use LaTeX in their Moodle site, so the LaTeX source will be in the web page. I hope this helps you to clarify your question. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: I do not know what OP wanted, but I have a question which may overlap. Is it possible to create questions off-line, for instance in an XML format, and then upload (import) them in bulk? I find it much faster to edit an XML file, than it is to use a web form, when I there is more than a question or two to create.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: George, Yes, in principal you can do this with STACK .  STACK uses the "moodle XML" format to import and export questions.  There are some sample questions here: https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/tree/master/samplequestions The form does have some sanitation checking of user's input, which is often a help. Pure XML does not have this, but does have other advantages, e.g. easy cut and paste between questions.  It has long been on my list to create a text-based mark up language for STACK, which abstracts as much as possible away so that over the longer term we can move closer to being able to share questions between platforms.  We are a long way from this, but it would be a start. This system has such a markup language ( https://sourceforge.net/projects/aimmath/files/latest/download?source=directory ) and WebWork does, although it is very tied to the underlying Perl language. If you have any success with this, or are able to engineer an alternative text based language, then I'd love to hear about it. Chris

ResponsesInList.Text: I'm having a little trouble getting the units to be recognized correctly on this STACK question that I've attached.  I'm wondering if this has to do with the fact that "g" is the only unit expected here because I haven't seen similar behavior on other questions. As an example, an answer might be 65.0g.  When that's entered, I get the following results: Input Insert Stars Strict Syntax Result Expected? 65.0g Yes Yes Invalid NO 65.0g Yes No Valid Yes 65.0g Yes, single character Yes Invalid NO 65.0g Yes, single character No Valid Yes If I edit the question to use "m" as the unit instead of "g" then 65.0m is valid Insert stars and strict syntax on. ResponsesInList.Title: STACK Issue with micrometers
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm trying to make a question using STACK that tests basic metric unit conversions.  To that end, I'm pulling random units from a list to go into the problem itself.  The entry in the list for μm is causing problems in the display of the question.  The entry in the list is `l1: [cm,mm,km,\mu*m]` This gives me things like this in the display when it gets used: Any suggestions?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: STACK Issue with micrometers
ResponsesInList.Text:
Joshua, Sorry about this confusion.  I think (without testing this....) that the problem is caused by the \mu in your list. The prefix for "micro" is just "u".  See https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/blob/master/stack/maxima/stackunits.mac#L32 So, your list should be 
```text
l1:[cm,mm,km,um]
```
 See also note (5) in https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/blob/master/doc/en/Authoring/Units.md If this doesn't fix the problem, please let me know. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: STACK Issue with micrometers
ResponsesInList.Text: That works fine for students entering "um" as their units.  They do indeed get interpreted and displayed as μm. However, in the question display that doesn't seem to work.  Instead I get just "um" displayed: That's better than where I was before but still not ideal.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: STACK Issue with micrometers
ResponsesInList.Text:
Sorry Joshua, I should have thought more carefully about this answer. You need to add the following to the start of your question variables. 
```text
stack_unit_si_declare(true)
```
 This is documented under the "units", but could have been more prominent. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: STACK Issue with micrometers
ResponsesInList.Text: Aha.  That worked perfectly. I see where that is in the documentation now.  From a usability standpoint, could that function just be automatically called whenever the Unit input type is used?

Can you give me a specific example of two things you are comparing, and what outcome you would like from NumSigFigs? ResponsesInList.Title: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello I'd like to write a STACK question as follows: "Consider the following limit: \(\lim_{x \to\infty} \frac{1}{x} + 2 + ...\) (etc.) Does this limit exist? [ans1 - True/false] If yes, enter its value: [ans2 - algebraic input]" There would be several (similar) variants of this question, looking almost identical to the student, where in some the limit exists and in some it does not. I can set up the two answer fields without problems, and check them within the PRT. However, I run into the following problem: In variants where the limit does exist, and hence ans2 appears in the response tree, Moodle requires that the student enters an answer for ans2 before processing the question. This gives away the answer to ans1 however. Is there some way to circumvent this? (Except for requiring the student to enter "value 1234" when the limit does not exist - I would like to avoid this.) Many thanks Henning

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: Henning, For now the only way to do this is to have more than one potential response tree, but this is not ideal. Colleagues in Finland are working on a much more adaptive model for STACK questions.  We plan to release this as version 4.  It will allow the question to adapt as you describe, plus a whole lot more. So, not now but in the future.  I'll ask them to comment in more detail. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: So I am one of those colleagues from Finland. While our system under development can do that we are still trying to figure out how to do it correctly. The current way how your case would be handled, in the stateful variant of STACK, depends on the ordering of the PRTs and some pretty annoying assumptions: The inputs not present/required (we can conditionally render them thus dropping it from the question text but that is not what you want, but can't drop them from the PRTs) for every variant would be handled in a separate PRT that may also tie to the other inputs but which would not have a specific point value. In that PRT we would only set a flag signalling that this part has been handled. The primary PRT would then include code that would check if that flag (not the actual input thus releasing the PRT from that input) is up and note it in the grading potentially simulating an incomplete answer by dropping penalties or something. The separate PRT handling the special input would have to be first in the question so that this would work. Problem is that the concept of STACKs PRTs requires all the inputs referenced in the PRT to be filled and that is something we would not want to mess with thus leading to trickery using state to transfer that information between PRTs. The problem with the current solution listed up there is that the system could not handle lowering that flag in the case where the student would erase that field as the flag (state) would only get modified when a PRT activates and it activates only if that field has a value. As to how I have been thinking this could be handled would be by giving PRTs the option of giving more than 100% of points maybe even negative points thus allowing you to have those inputs in separate PRTs and could coordinate the grading between them without knowing the value of the other input in the PRT. This would mainly be used to handle the cases where we use different PRTs depending on the students actions i.e. the stateful variant tends to be used to build questions where the student has optional paths and has to choose between them leading to problems when we can't give points that were not achievable as they existed on the other paths not taken. Anyway, in the stateful variant your question could be posed first as a single boolean asking if the limit exists and depending on that answer we could ask another question about its value but the questions would probably not be visible on the screen at the same time. Currently you could use Moodle to randomise between two questions both looking exactly the same outwards but the other would have a fake input and the other a real one i.e. the other would be the no-case and in that the input would not be referenced by the PRT. Finally, what your example really needs is not stateful it just needs a multiple choice input type with other as an option, you would then ask for the value of the limit with a multiple choice that has "no value" as an option some possible wrong options and that other-field to either distract or accept the actual value. MCQ inputs are relatively new for STACK and I understand that this in on the wish list already.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Chris, Matti, thanks for your answers. I'm not sure whether I was successful in describing the problem though... My query has nothing to do with multiple choice inputs (the students are supposed to enter the value of the limit algebraically). I'm not asking to hide the second input field depending on the state of the first one (a redundant input field is fine). It's also not to do with combining the "limit exists" and "limit does not exist" variants into one STACK question - I'm quite happy with having several different but (optically) similar questions, and randomizing between these. The actual problem arises in a question where the limit *exists* (but where the student doesn't a priori know that it does). To the student, the question reads: "Consider the following limit: ... Does this limit exist? [ans1 - True/false] If yes, enter its value: [ans2 - algebraic input]" When the student answers "True" for ans1, the question works as expected. However, when the student (incorrectly) enters "False", and submits the answer, then they get the message "Please answer all parts of the question." This of course gives away the fact that their answer to ans1 is incorrect. Following Matti's suggestion, I tried to use two response trees, one depending on "ans1" and one depending on "ans2", where the one for "ans1" has zero point value. However, the same behaviour occurs. Maybe there's another workaround that I haven't figured out yet? Best wishes Henning

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry about my unclear answer I do not mean that you should do a MCQ but you could use such an input to merge the two inputs your question requires as a single input. Something like this (options would be "No limit" and "Limit is ______"), problem is that STACK has no such input type yet. Naturally, you could simply have a single algebraic input that asks for the limits value or some specific keyword if no value exists. What I suggest is that you think if you could live with a question that does not ask separately about the existence of the limit and the value if it exists and instead just asks for the value with the option of signalling the nonexistence with a special value. Thus simplifying the two tightly bound questions to one that fits to the PRT-model of STACK. Currently there exists no other way for handling what you ask for as the PRTs cannot handle the situation where not all inputs are used. The problem from the questions side is that if there exists an input for the limit it can't handle the situation where that input would not be used as at the very least there will be a portion of points that will be tied to that input and can't be given if the input remains empty. The current STACK cannot change the structure of PRTs based on the questions parameters so it just can't be made to forget about that input.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matti, thanks for clarifying. The workaround that I found now (though slightly imperfect) is to allow "none" as an "allowed word" in the ans2 field, and to set the syntax hint for the field to "none"; I can then treat ans2 as a required field in all variants of the question, The example question suggested using "1111" as a special value for "limit does not exist" but that was (rightfully) criticized by some colleagues as confusing; using  "none" as a special value alone, without the true/false box, would have meant that students lose marks if they mistype "none" (or they type "no" instead), which is also somewhat confusing. Best wishes Henning

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Optional answer fields in STACK?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Henning, I was musing over this problem for the last few days as well. I agree 11111 is an awful hack to this problem! Actually, I think your "none" is very close indeed to what I was about to suggest. We really have to actively distinguish an empty input box (passive) where the student has done nothing, from the situation where a student has chosen to say "none"  (active).  So I'd argue that allowing none is a very sensible suggestion here. I think this is also an ideal situation to use the new "Disappearing syntax hint".  (I'll merge and release this during the summer sometime, before the next academic session.) https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/issues/211 Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Support for scientific units in STACK: numerical tests
ResponsesInList.Text: I've pushed some prototype code to a new branch: https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/tree/ATUnitsNum This implements new answer tests which combine support for scientific units with two more numerical answer tests, NumAbsolute and NumRelative.  On reflection, I'm not sure how useful UnitsAbsolute will actually be in situations where the student has compatible units.  See the docs for an explanation of this. I've not added in the "decimal places" answer test, as significant work needs to be done on the underlying numerical test before this is truly reliable. In particular the decimal places test is implemented, and the code works, however it cannot be used in STACK because of difficulties with validation. To fully implement this we need an "ephemeral form" for floating point numbers, which will require some more work. I'd really like to receive some test cases from science teachers to test this, particularly in edge cases involving awkward numerical rounding.  This is not my area of expertise, so comments and tests very welcome.  When people are happy with this I'll merge this back with the master branch for release. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm in the process of adding in support for answers with scientific units into STACK . I'm posting on the list to ask for help in the *design* of these features.  I'm not asking for help writing code, I'll do that!  What I do need is some advice from people who regularly teach mathematics with units.  E.g. science and engineering. I've posted a working prototype of the code in the branch "units".  See https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/tree/units Those of you able to do so are welcome to test out this branch yourselves. The support for adding units has been written by Matti Harjula in Aalto.  Thanks Matti!  This code is listed on https://github.com/maths/moodle-qtype_stack/blob/units/stack/maxima/stackunits.mac The current basic behaviour, with some example feedback is shown below.  I really could use a lot more test cases, particularly from physics and chemistry where there are a variety of units. Please email me with comments, and examples to C.J.Sangwin@ed.ac.uk. This is an opportunity for people who will use this feature to influence the design.  If you ask for something, you might even get it before the design is released and fixed! Some questions Do you want a separate input type to enable answers without units, for example, to be rejected as invalid?  Currently, student must use the algebraic input.  If so, how should this work?  E.g. no units=invalid, wrong units=valid. I've used the existing NumSigFigs test as the numerical test with which to check the numerical accuracy.  Is this the right test to use?  STACK has a number of numerical tests, so I chose this one. The current plan is to test this over the next month, and then together with some other new features (including multiple choice inputs), release an incremental version at the end of January. In parallel to this there are a number of other things going on, including "reasoning by equivalence" which I've mentioned before. I've been asked about support for scientific units for some time, so this seemed worthwhile releasing as an increment sooner. Chris Sample input-output behavious Passed? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: This is incredibly exciting.  I thoroughly confused my wife earlier with a big giant fist pump when I saw this. I teach high school chemistry and here are my thoughts: As far as grading goes, I have always made a small point deduction when students have forgotten units or used the wrong units.  The current numerical question type in standard Moodle has always matched up well with this. If having a separate input type would mean that students wouldn't have to use the * to include the units then that would be excellent.  That's training the students that shouldn't really have to happen if its possible. I would leave off the feedback note " ATUnits_compatible_units" if the answer gets full credit.  It is still useful when it is incorrect but would only serve to confuse students otherwise. On the 12.45*m/s student answer in your tests, I would suggest that it also give some feedback that its more than just a sigfig issue.  The answer is not the same as 12.3*m/s. There are times when my questions ask for specific units because I want to make sure that students are clear on the unit conversions themselves.  Requiring specific units and disallowing SI prefix conversions in the answer tests should be a feature. There are times where we have quantities that are unitless (pH, equilibrium constants) that it would be nice if everything looked the same to students and it would be able to give appropriate feedback if they put in units that they were not supposed to include. Case-sensitivity is important as I use problems early on for testing unit conversions that could have both mL and ML in them (milliliters and megaliters).  Also, m (meters) and M (molarity). Chemistry uses some non-standard pseudo units on a pretty regular basis that it would be nice to be able to still use.  It is also typical for us to use English units in the US when first teaching unit conversions.  Here are some units that I use in my class.  These do NOT include all the SI prefix variations. m ft inches miles g amu pounds s min hr days weeks years L cups pints quarts gallons mol mole moles (yes students enter all of these) K °C Hz 1/s kPa atm mmHg Torr bar J M atoms molecules ions formula units It is also not at all uncommon to see units reported as "g H 2 O".  We've already discussed how hard that is so I wouldn't bother with this issue

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Joshua, I've removed the feedback you suggested wasn't sensible and kept the note.  This is committed. "On the 12.45*m/s student answer in your tests, I would suggest that it also give some feedback that its more than just a sigfig issue.  The answer is not the same as 12.3*m/s." Agreed, but actually this was a very poorly chosen example on my part!  The option [3,2] means, check the answer is to 3 sig figs, only two of which need to agree.  So these options are accurate.  If you give ans answer something like 13.45*m/s then the feedback is "Your answer contains the wrong number of significant digits. The accuracy of your answer is not correct...." Thank you for pointing this out though, I've added another test case to clarify this. Having read these comments I suggest the following way of working, but would value further comments. (1) I create a new "input type" (Units). this will be one input box like "Algebraic" because its easier to implement. if we have two input boxes (as Daniel suggests), then what happens if a student puts units in the wrong one? (They will!) there is nothing stopping a teacher using two inputs to separate out these things if they choose to. A teacher should use existing "insert stars" option, as now, to avoid having to type in "*", which is silly here. Joshua said "There are times where we have quantities that are unitless (pH, equilibrium constants) that it would be nice if everything looked the same to students and it would be able to give appropriate feedback if they put in units that they were not supposed to include." Ok, how about we can have the "units" input type infer from the teacher's answer whether or not the student is supposed to use units? If the teacher supplies a number with units, the student *must* use some kind of units, otherwise their answer is invalid. If the teacher just supplies a number, so must the student.  If the student uses units, this will be invalid. In this case, the PRT will *not* use the units answer test, which expects units (obviously!) I think this is a good example of where separating validity and correctness helps a lot (without a student loosing marks on a technicality: no unit, unwanted units) (2) Partial credit.  We are never going to agree on partial credit, so I think teachers who want to award this need to write more complex PRTs. So far STACK hasn't enabled teachers to award partial credit through the answer tests, and I'm very nervous about starting to do so now. This is the job of the Potential Response trees. There is already a function which splits up the student's answer into a list [number, units] So, many of the situations can be dealt with using these things separately in a PRT with many nodes. [I'll reconsider this position if someone can sketch out a very simple and easy to use mechanism for indicating partial credit in this case.] (3) I'll develop some mechanism to let teachers add in custom units, relevant to that question, with conversion factors. - if you want/need "rods, poles and perches" so be it. - We already have pre-defined families of sensible ones, e.g. see the options on "Forbidden words".  There are tags here for common lists. ** Other issues "There are times when my questions ask for specific units because I want to make sure that students are clear on the unit conversions themselves.  Requiring specific units and disallowing SI prefix conversions in the answer tests should be a feature." In this case, Input validation: use the units input to make sure the student has some. PRT node 1: use the units answer test to check the student is correct (accuracy and units). PRT node 2: if PRT node 1 is true (the student is correct), check the units are exact. If not, award no marks with feedback? I think this should work, and will leave sensible notes for later analysis.  We could add an option to the answertest, but that is akward as I've already used the answer test options field for the numerical accuracy. Another option here is to have more than one answer test, e.g. Strict units Equivalent units Would that be more useful? STACK is case sensitive, so mL and ML should be ok.  I'll add unit tests for this.... I've no plans to support chemical formulae like H 2 O anytime soon! C

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay Chris I have my test server loaded now and can see a little more what you are doing. You are correct that by using two different boxes a teacher should be able to sort out equivalence of differing unit systems through the potential response trees. This already possible by treating units as variables and doing algebraic equivalence tests. As it appears to me now you are really attempting to make a simpler way for science teachers to make comparisons of units as STACK does using scientific notation. If this is your goal, then restricting your efforts to the common SI units is probably worthwhile and sufficient (as much fun as converting cubits to barleycorn might be). There are a lot of units in science that this approach  would not fit. in addition to pH, there are temperature (Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kelvin), pressure, decibels, foot candles etc. in which simple proportionality is not the appropriate conversion method. At the moment I do not understand some of the feedback.  If a teacher provides 10 kg as the model answer and the student answers 100 g. I would think the units are correct in the students response (mass), but that the calculation is off by two orders of magnitude. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Apologies for coming to this discussion rather late and also for the fact that I haven't read all the discussion in detail. I just want to highlight a few issues that we've had at the Open University in checking and giving feedback on units on various interdisciplinary science and physics modules (mostly from OpenMark). I am really pleased you're introducing a unit check into STACK; in my experience, the most common errors that our students make are with units (even more so than with sig figs). However, it is important that students are given appropriate targeted feedback - they get very upset if told they are wrong when it is 'just' the units that are wrong. I like the idea of no units being invalid whilst incorrect units are valid (but wrong). I have been surprised that students do not usually omit units; they do usually get them wrong! My only issue with this approach would be if an answer is correctly dimensionless, and one of the things you want is for students to realize this. I am pleased that the multiplication doesn't have to be explicitly stated, because although this is mathematically correct it isn't how units are usually written. Someone has asked about spaces before units. We encourage this in written work, but for automatic checking we strip out all spaces - otherwise I suspect we would get even more complaints. Similarly, someone has mentioned that units shouldn't be italic. Correct, but I wouldn't worry. In an ideal world, I would like teacher choice over: whether e.g. 25 g and 0.025 kg are treated as equivalent, or whether you insist on an answer in SI base units (kg on this occasion). whether you accept e.g. m/s and m s^(-1) as equivalent, or demand one or the other. whether you accept e.g. N and kg m s^(-2) as equivalent. Whether you accept units in non-conventional non-simplified form (which you will get!) whether you mark them as correct. I hope this helps. Sally

ResponsesInList.Text: Sally, Thanks for these comments.  I think we are close to your "ideal world" already.... (1) There are two answer tests Unit and UnitStrict.  The first thinks 25 g and 0.025 kg are equivalent and the latter thinks they are not. (2)  I had hoped that whether you accept e.g. m/s and m*s^(-1) as equivalent could be checked with the "EqualsComAss" test as a separate property. But, the function stack_units_split(ex); is needed to split the units from the number, and this function (necessarily) subtly changes m*s^(-1) to m/s....  So you can't.  I've added this to the TODO list. (3) Same as (1). (4) Hadn't thought about this.  Thanks.  This is a good point.  Currently both Unit and UnitStrict think that 9.81*m/s/s and -9.81*m/s^2 are the same (to 3 sig figs).  I think this is related to (2).  Currently UnitStrict uses "algebraic equivalence" to compare units.  Unit makes substitutions, then uses algebraic equivalence.  If there is demand, I'll add this feature later. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, Thanks very much for all this work and opportunity for discussion. Like Sally I haven't read all the previous discussions in detail, but here are a few comments/thoughts. Units can open various cans-of-worms: during our recent production of maths modules at the Open University I've been involved with we had (nearly!) endless discussion about this, and I am very aware different (sub-)disciplines have different traditions in this respect. I don't think I'll be (immediately) using any new Unit functionality (possibly because we would want all questions within a module to behave similarly, and I'm not changing them all now!) but I do see the advantage of this. I'm sure its something that my colleagues in Engineering and Science (including Sally) would like! 1) I'd support having a separate unit-aware version of the numerical answer type, rather than using the algebraic type. I think answers involving units will always be numerical (or something that evaluates to a numerical expression). I personally don't like answers such as "x m" (where x is a variable and m means metres). In such a case I think the units (hence dimension) are part of the variable. In a question stem I would write "distance x (in m)" rather than expecting an answer of the form "x m". Of course, this then brings in the other philosophical issue that "x" measured in metres is different (but somehow the same!) as the same "x" measured in km. [Here lies the first can-of-worms.......] I guess I'm saying that in a unit answer type, all "letters" are interpreted as units? Expect (noting one of your earlier comments) I would tend to permit "sqrt(2) m" if appropriate to the question. 2) I won't like students to have to enter  2*m,  but rather 2m or 2[space]m (both should be permitted?). As as been mentioned, the existing "automatically insert stars" code should sort that.  More problematical is that I would also prefer ms^-1 to m*s^-1, which the current insert stars could would not resolve. (And yes, we do tend to use this in preference to m/s, for no obvious reason!) The use of m for "metre" and "milli" might also cause difficulties? 3)  I guess  1+2m would be accepted as 3m, which I would be happy with, but some might think it ought to be 1m+2m. (Similarly, some groups at the OU like showing units for each number in each line of working in a calculation, but I (and maths generally, I guess strictly incorrectly) tend to just deal with the numbers as stick the unit back in the final result.) 4) I agree that the issue of part-marks for wrong units (assuming they get past the above suggested validation checks!) should be done within the PRT. 5) If some questions in a quiz involve units and others don't, students are going to type units were they are not wanted, and not include them when they are! So  I would like the presence (or not) of a unit to be checked at the input validation stage rather than loosing marks for it.  One could given go a step further and (optionally) check the dimension of the units at this stage too?! 6) The ability to turn on or off the acceptance of equivalent units sounds worthwhile, and if off it would seem only fair to flag a wrong unit at the validation stage too? 7) I have a recollection that the OU's OpenMark system might have support for units, the behaviour of which might be of some help? (Tim H would know more). Similarly, Maxima has a "units" package,  ....../share/physics/units.mac  but that doesn't seem particularly robust: m/s returns "meter/s" and "ms^-1" returns "1000000.0/second" !! Best wishes, Tim

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Tim for your comments,  very helpful, (1) There is broad agreement that (for now) any letters which occur as part of an answer will be considered as "units", i.e. x*m is not allowed, but will be valid. (2.1) ms is "milliseconds" so ms^-1 is 1/ms.  This is a useful unit, so we have to be strict with m*s^-1 for m/s.  Of course, there are already ways round this: (a) forbid "ms" in a particular input, (b) use single letter variables names to split ms^-1 to m*s^-1. (2.2) I'm really reluctant to have spaces for implied multiplication! (3) 1+2m is currently invalid with feedback.  At some point students need to learn to be precise.  We *could* change the binding power of + vs * but that will cause havoc elsewhere..... (5) I've no intention of adding in a check to confirm "compatiable" units at the validation stage for the first round of this feature, but have added it to the list for the future.  If there is real demand I'll add it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Chris, I really think you need to reconsider the spaces and multiplication issue.  I don't train my students at all on how they need to enter units into my Moodle questions now but the vast majority of them use spaces between the number and unit. I picked one of my earliest homework assignments and ran some stats on it.  Of the 113 final responses, 88 used a space between the number and unit.  Only 12 didn't use a space.  The other 13 were missing units (there is a penalty and this in adaptive mode).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: It seems like I have to come and say something about the way we designed that code and have used in Aalto and in TKK before Aalto, but lets start with these points in this comment first: I don't think answers will always be purely numerical and my favourite counter example for this is an abstract inclined plane type of a question where the angle of the plane is not defined but everything else is thus leaving some symbolic things like "sin(alpha)" and "cos(alpha)" to be inputted in the answers which otherwise might be anything from meters to Newtons. But I do agree that if the answer contains "x" that "x" will not have an unit inside itself. Due to that "cos(alpha)" edge case we can't interpret all letters as units and we should actually use our knowledge about the defined units to only identify them as units and leave everything else to the non unit side. As Chris said "ms" is milliseconds and that is that also handling spaces in the input is a larger problem and I do side with Chris although my opinion is that students should just learn to input things in exact form so that the computers can understand them. (On the other hand in my opinion every student should be required to code a RPN calculator on their own before they get to complain about syntax in anything. Considering that I might require it to be coded in Piet to make sure that the lesson will be remembered.) The use "m" the prefix and "m" the unit are not causing problems as prefixes do not exist alone in this system the prefixes are fixed to the units and the only interesting case would be with multi letter units if we had an unit with symbol "aa" and we then defined another unit with symbol "a" then we would have a prefix problem as we could not know if "aa" is atto-a or just aa. Not accepted, mixed units in the sum. Unitles + meters makes no sense. Again I won't repeat what Chris said about this. Couldn't agree more. I don't really understand this but I think even this can be done in the PRT as you can tune the penalties there. In general the physics people that have used this units code and its previous versions for the last five or more years here do not really care in what units you answer as long as the answer converts to the correct answer and I would therefore consider the turning of the acceptance of equivalent units as an edge case that could be left to the PRT side. Especially as I think requiring specific units to be used is something that typically requires customised feedback that is what I have heard from the health related fields. Yes maxima has plenty of units packages but they tend to contain plenty of presentation related features that do not really interest us and tend to be overly complex for our needs. Your example of using milliseconds here is again an example how these things can work very oddly as in them the prefixes are typically case-insensitive and the "m" prefix might mean anything and actually getting e.g. millimeters may require you to write the whole thing out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Support for scientific units in STACK.
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Tim and Matti. I accept all your responses! (In OU courses we tend to use the latex "\," between a number a unit.) Re Chris' reply 2.1: I think the "insert stars" code will convert  ms^-1 to (m*s)^-1 not the m(s^-1) that is meant!
